name: io.github.KalarisLabs/kuchi
title: Kuchi
description: Pick a real launch video as a template, get its frame-by-frame breakdown and plan your own remake.

tools.name: kuchi_get_workflow
tools.description:
Get Kuchi's workflow for turning a reference into the user's own launch video: how to pick a reference, how to analyse each shot from the storyboard sheets, what to ask the user for, how to match timing to the frame, and how to check the result against the reference.

Returns Markdown. Pass step to get one step ("find", "study", "plan", "build" or "check") with the rules that hold for all of them, or leave it out for the whole workflow. Read it before a first remake; the other tools return the data each step works on.

step.description: 'all' (default) for the whole workflow, or one step: 'find', 'study', 'plan', 'build' or 'check'

tools.name: kuchi_suggest_templates
tools.description:
Get a short list of Kuchi launch videos for the user to choose their template from, ranked against what they want and what they can supply.

Pass what is known: a few words on the product and the feel wanted, preferred styles, theme, pace, aspect ratio, target length and the kinds of asset the user has. All are optional, and they rank rather than filter. Returns up to 6 numbered choices, each with what fits, what differs, what the user would need to supply, a poster and a watch link; a recommended choice; a question to put to the user; and the gallery link, where the user can pick any video and paste its link instead.

Use it when the user wants a launch video and has not picked a reference. Use kuchi_search_videos to browse or filter the whole library.

looking_for.description: A few words on the product and the feel wanted, e.g. 'AI note-taking app, calm and premium'

styles.description: Preferred motion styles, e.g. ['UI motion', 'Kinetic type']; kuchi_list_filters has the full list

available_assets.description: The kinds of asset the user can supply. Templates that need something else rank lower and say so.

exclude.description: Videos the user has already turned down

items.description: A Kuchi video id ('34'), slug, Kuchi link (https://kuchi.kalarislabs.com/#video-34) or the original X post URL

response_format.description: 'markdown' (default) for readable text, 'json' for structured data

tools.name: kuchi_search_videos
tools.description:
Search Kuchi's launch-video references by product type, brand, motion style, format, pace, theme, aspect ratio or length.

Returns one page of videos with notes on their motion, measured rhythm (shots, pace, theme), a poster image, a storyboard sheet and a playable Kuchi link. Use kuchi_list_filters for valid filter values, kuchi_get_video for one video's details and kuchi_get_breakdown for its shot list.

Examples:
  - "dark cinematic AI launch" -> query="AI", theme="dark"
  - "a short vertical teaser" -> aspect_ratio="9:16", max_seconds=20
  - "launch videos built from app UI" -> style="UI motion"
  - "fast-cut launch with charts" -> pace="fast", style="Charts"

query.description: Keywords matched against titles, brands, styles, formats, motion notes and shot descriptions

style.description: Exact motion style, e.g. 'UI motion', 'Kinetic type', 'Device motion'

category.description: Exact category, e.g. 'AI launch', 'Feature clip', 'Startup launch'

pace.description: Measured cutting pace: slow is under 1.5 shot changes per 10 s, rapid is 7 or more

max_seconds.description: Only videos at most this long

response_format.description: 'markdown' (default) for readable text, 'json' for structured data

tools.name: kuchi_get_video
tools.description: Get one Kuchi reference by id, slug, Kuchi link or X post URL: playable video file, poster, storyboard sheet, length, size, aspect ratio, styles, measured rhythm and notes on its motion. Use kuchi_search_videos to find ids and kuchi_get_breakdown for the shot list.

reference.description: A Kuchi video id ('34'), slug, Kuchi link (https://kuchi.kalarislabs.com/#video-34) or the original X post URL

response_format.description: 'markdown' (default) for readable text, 'json' for structured data

tools.name: kuchi_list_filters
tools.description: List every motion style, category, format, aspect ratio, pace and theme in Kuchi, with how many videos each has, to use as filters in kuchi_search_videos. Also lists the shot kinds a shot is classified into when you analyse a storyboard.

response_format.description: 'markdown' (default) for readable text, 'json' for structured data

tools.name: kuchi_get_breakdown
tools.description:
Get the shot-by-shot breakdown of one Kuchi reference, measured from every frame of its video file.

Returns exact facts (fps, frame count, length), every shot's start and end in seconds and frames, how it enters (cut, animated transition, hold or blank frame), how much of the frame moves, its tone and colors, motion and loudness per second, and storyboard sheets: grids of real frames stamped with their time and shot number. Each shot says where to see it: its frame on the overview sheet, when it has one, and the detail sheets that show it.

Kuchi measures when things happen; what each shot shows is read from the frames. The result lists the shot kinds to classify against, and the analysis goes to kuchi_plan_remake as shot_analysis.

Set storyboard="overview" (one frame per shot, or per longest shot when there are many) or "detail" (evenly spaced frames that cover every shot, page with detail_sheet) to receive that sheet as an image. Use it before kuchi_plan_remake to study a reference, and while building to match each shot.

reference.description: A Kuchi video id ('34'), slug, Kuchi link (https://kuchi.kalarislabs.com/#video-34) or the original X post URL

storyboard.description: 'links' (default) returns sheet URLs only; 'overview' or 'detail' also returns one sheet as an image

detail_sheet.description: Which detail sheet to return when storyboard="detail" (1 is the start of the video)

shot_offset.description: Shots to skip, for videos with many shots

response_format.description: 'markdown' (default) for readable text, 'json' for structured data

tools.name: kuchi_plan_remake
tools.description:
Plan a launch video for the user's product, using a Kuchi reference as an inspiration template.

Pass the user's own product details and assets, and your shot_analysis: the kind of each reference shot, read from the storyboard sheets of kuchi_get_breakdown. Returns what to borrow from the reference (rhythm, color roles, motion), a blueprint that re-times the reference's shots to the target length on whole frames and says what content of the user's goes in each shot, the rules for using a reference, and missing_inputs: questions to ask the user before building. ready=false means required inputs are missing. Shots without a kind keep their exact timing and get placeholder content.

Call it again with the user's answers and your analysis until ready=true and every shot has a kind. Only list assets the user actually gave you. It does not render video; build it with your own tools, then call kuchi_check_remake.

reference.description: A Kuchi video id ('34'), slug, Kuchi link (https://kuchi.kalarislabs.com/#video-34) or the original X post URL

product_name.description: The user's product name. Without it, the plan asks for it in missing_inputs.

product_description.description: What the product does and who it is for, in the user's words

key_features.description: 1-3 features or moments to show, most important first

call_to_action.description: The closing line or URL, e.g. 'Try it at acme.com'

assets.description: Assets the user has provided. Only list assets the user actually gave you.

description.description: What it shows, e.g. 'Dashboard, dark mode'

location.description: URL or file path, if the user gave one. Kuchi never opens it.

shot_analysis.description: Your reading of the reference's shots from its storyboard sheets. One entry per shot; send as many as you have analysed.

shot.description: The reference shot's number, from kuchi_get_breakdown

kind.description: What the shot is; kuchi_get_breakdown describes each kind

shows.description: One line on what is on screen and where it sits, e.g. 'Dashboard centered, sidebar left, cursor moves to a button'

target_seconds.description: Target length in seconds; defaults to the reference's length

fps.description: Frame rate you will render at, e.g. 30 or 60; defaults to the reference's. The blueprint's frame numbers use it.

aspect_ratio.description: Output ratio; defaults to the reference's

sound.description: How the video sounds: 'sfx' (open-license sound effects on each shot's cue, the default), 'music_and_sfx' (an open-license music bed too), 'user_track' (the user's own music or voiceover, the default when assets include one) or 'silent'

shot_offset.description: Blueprint shots to skip, for references with many shots

response_format.description: 'markdown' (default) for readable text, 'json' for structured data

tools.name: kuchi_check_remake
tools.description:
Check a drafted or finished remake against the rules for using a Kuchi reference.

Pass your shot list: timing, the reference shot each one rebuilds, how it enters, the on-screen text, and where each asset came from. Flags text that carries over the reference's brand, assets taken from the reference, generated logos or product UI, placeholders, timing gaps, and shots whose length or entrance drifted from the reference shot they rebuild. Also returns compare_frames: the exact time in your video and in the reference that show the same moment, to set side by side. passed=false means there are errors to fix.

It checks what you report, not the rendered file: Kuchi never receives your video. Be accurate about each asset's source.

reference.description: A Kuchi video id ('34'), slug, Kuchi link (https://kuchi.kalarislabs.com/#video-34) or the original X post URL

product_name.description: The user's product name, to check it appears on screen

target_seconds.description: The length you were aiming for

music_source.description: Where the music came from: 'none' when there is no music (sound effects alone are reported as assets)

start_s.description: When the shot starts in your video, in seconds

reference_shot.description: The reference shot this one rebuilds (the blueprint's reference_shot). Needed for the timing check and compare_frames.

enters.description: How this shot enters in your video

on_screen_text.description: Every line of text visible in this shot

kind.description: What the asset is; a sound effect is 'sound_effect'

source.description: 'user' = the user supplied it; 'stock' = an open-license or licensed library file; 'reference' = taken from the Kuchi reference video

description.description: What it is, for your own notes. Kuchi does not keep it.

response_format.description: 'markdown' (default) for readable text, 'json' for structured data

tools.name: kuchi_list_components
tools.description:
List Kuchi's copy-paste Remotion video components: animated text and kinetic type, captions, AI-input and UI screens, cursors, logos, scenes and transitions. It is the set on https://kuchi.kalarislabs.com/components, read from the latest published registry.

Returns one page of components, each with its name, title, what it animates, category, npm and Kuchi dependencies, files, registry URL and shadcn install command, plus every category with its count. Filter by keywords or category. Shared library code that components build on is left out unless category="library". Use kuchi_get_component for one component's source.

Use it while building a remake, to find a ready-made component for a shot before writing one from scratch.

query.description: Keywords matched against names, titles and descriptions, e.g. 'typewriter', 'captions', 'chat prompt'

category.description: Exact category, e.g. 'text', 'scenes', 'screens', 'ai-input', 'captions', 'cursor', 'logos' or 'library'; the result lists them all

response_format.description: 'markdown' (default) for readable text, 'json' for structured data

tools.name: kuchi_get_component
tools.description:
Get one Kuchi video component by name: its description, npm and Kuchi dependencies, shadcn install command, registry URL, usage notes and the full source of its files, read from the latest published registry.

Returns one file's source per call (file=1 is the main file); a file longer than about 20k characters comes in parts, and the result says which file and part comes next. Kuchi components it depends on (such as kuchi-ui) are components of their own: get each the same way, or use the install command, which fetches them too. Use kuchi_list_components to find names.

name.description: Component name from kuchi_list_components, e.g. 'text-reveal', or its registry URL (https://kuchi.kalarislabs.com/r/text-reveal.json)

file.description: Which file to return the source of (1-based, default 1)

part.description: Which part of a long file to return (default 1)

response_format.description: 'markdown' (default) for readable text, 'json' for structured data

tools.name: kuchi_get_skill
tools.description:
Get one of Kuchi's agent skills: step-by-step methods for the build and finish of a remake, bundled with the server so every client has them.

- kuchi: the whole remake workflow in short (find, study, plan, build, check).
- kuchi-product-launch-video: the whole job of making a product launch video, from the brief to the delivered MP4 (brief, choose a reference, study, plan, storyboard, build, sound, check, render per platform). Start here when the user wants a launch video.
- kuchi-remotion: building the blueprint in Remotion: project setup, the @ alias Kuchi components need, one Sequence per shot, entrances, fonts, assets, rendering and exporting frames to compare.
- kuchi-sound: sound without hearing it: turning each blueprint shot's sound cue into an open-license sound effect (or the user's track) placed on its frame, chosen and trimmed by measuring with ffmpeg, with every license logged.
- kuchi-audio-check: measuring the rendered mix: loudness, true peak, clipping, silence and whether each sound lands on its cue frame.

Returns the skill's Markdown. Use kuchi-product-launch-video when a launch video is asked for, and the others before writing video code (kuchi-remotion), before adding audio (kuchi-sound) and before delivering (kuchi-audio-check).

tools.name: search
tools.description: Search Kuchi launch-video references. Returns ids to pass to fetch. Same catalog as kuchi_search_videos.

tools.name: fetch
tools.description: Fetch one Kuchi reference by the id from search, with its notes, links and metadata.

tools.name: kuchi_send_feedback
tools.description: Send feedback about this server to its developers: a capability you needed that no tool provides, a tool that failed or misled you, or something that worked well. Records the feedback; it does not add or change tools. Leave out personal or sensitive details.

feedback_type.description: What kind of feedback this is. Use 'missing_capability' when the tool you needed does not exist in the tool list - nothing failed, the capability is absent. Use 'issue' when an existing tool behaved badly: it failed, returned a confusing error, or its description or schema misled you. Use 'praise' when something worked notably well. Use 'other' for anything else.

summary.description: One self-contained sentence. For 'missing_capability': the capability you needed, e.g. 'No way to filter videos by music genre.' For 'issue': the tool and the problem, e.g. 'kuchi_get_breakdown returned no storyboard for video 90.'

details.description: Optional longer context: what you tried, exact parameter values, the error text you saw, and any workaround you used. Omit when the summary says it all.

friction_points.description: Optional: the specific moments that slowed you down, as short bullet-like sentences, quoting exact tool names, parameters, or error text.

suggested_improvement.description: Optional: the concrete change that would have helped, e.g. the tool to add, the description to reword, or the error message to improve.

tool_name.description: Optional: the existing tool this feedback is about (for 'issue' or 'praise'). Leave empty for 'missing_capability' - the point is that no tool fits.

sentiment.description: Optional: how the experience felt overall.

task_completed.description: Optional: whether you still completed the user's task despite the problem.
